headline: Brazilian Real Hits Six-Month Low Ahead of US Labor Data
summary: The Brazilian real depreciated to a six-month low against the US dollar. The move occurred as markets awaited US employment data and following the central bank's decision to maintain the Selic rate at 13.75%.
why: The Brazilian real is the primary currency of Latin America's largest economy. Its value is sensitive to interest rate differentials between Brazil and the US, as well as global risk sentiment.
why_moved: The currency weakened due to the combination of local interest rate policy and anticipation of US economic data, which influences global capital flows.
